learning_outcomes.text: Possess and understand knowledge that provides a basis or opportunity to be original in the development and/or application of ideas, often in a research context.
Students know how to apply the acquired knowledge and their problem-solving ability in new or unfamiliar environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their area of study.

Students are able to integrate knowledge and deal with the complexity of formulating judgments based on incomplete or limited information, including reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
Students know how to communicate their conclusions and the knowledge and ultimate reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences in a clear and unambiguous way.
Students possess the learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a way that will largely be self-directed or autonomous.

Have adequate knowledge of the scientific and technological aspects of: mathematical, analytical and numerical methods in engineering, electrical engineering, energy engineering, chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, continuum mechanics, industrial electronics, automation, manufacturing, materials, quantitative management methods, industrial informatics, urban planning and infrastructures.
Plan, calculate and design products, processes, facilities and plants.
Conduct research, development and innovation in products, processes and methods.
Carry out strategic planning and apply it to construction and production, quality and environmental management systems.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the Industrial Engineer profession.
Knowledge and capacity for the analysis and design of electrical power generation, transmission and distribution systems.
Knowledge and capabilities for the design and analysis of thermal machines and engines, hydraulic machines and industrial heating and cooling installations.
Knowledge and capabilities that allow understanding, analyzing, exploiting and managing the different energy sources.
Know the energy policy guidelines and advanced technologies for thermoelectric generation with minimal pollutant emissions.
Apply, evaluate and analyze clean thermoelectric generation technologies under different technical possibilities according to the types of applications.
Select and apply technologies for reducing pollutant emissions in combustion gases.

syllabus_topics: Energy planning for the reduction of polluting emissions
Basic circuits in a thermal power plant
Clean technologies. SC and USC thermal power plants
Clean technologies. Integrated Gasification Combined Cycle
Sources of polluting emissions in thermoelectric generation
Combustion process analysis: Combustion balance of a fuel
Combustion process analysis: Determination of boiler efficiency in a thermal power plant
Combustion process analysis: Emission balance in a thermal power plant
Combined cycle thermal power plant analysis
teaching_methods: Non-contact work (Virtual Campus activities, autonomous work)

assessment_methods.method: Practical evaluation tests (PL) - Laboratory and computer lab practices

assessment_rules: For ordinary and extraordinary calls, the final grade (NF) is calculated as NF = N*0.6 + PC*0.10 + PL*0.3, where N is the exam grade, PC is class participation, and PL is the average of practical evaluation tests. Incorrect answers on the written exam are penalized. No minimum grade is required for any evaluable element. For differentiated evaluation, the final grade is NF = N*0.7 + PL*0.3, with a final theory exam weighted at 70% and a final practical exam weighted at 30%.
